newsitem.title: USA: US senators to press energy nominee on nuke waste.
newsitem.headline: US senators to press energy nominee on nuke waste.

text.p: Senate Energy Committee chairman Frank Murkowski urged President Bill Clinton Wednesday to pick an energy secretary who would be willing to find a way to start taking spent nuclear fuel away from utilities.

"You should know that we and other members of the committee will make this a key point of questioning during confirmation hearings for your nominee," Republicans Murkowski of Alaska and Sen. Larry Craig of Idaho said in a December 18 letter to Clinton.
The leading candidate to replace Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary is believed to be Elizabeth Moler, chairwoman of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
"Allowing radioactive materials to continue piling up near our homes, schools and neighborhoods is highly irresponsible," the senators said.

The letter came on the heels of a notice from the Energy Department to utilities saying it would not be able to start accepting spent fuel from their nuclear reactors by Jan 31, 1998 as required under law, and asking them for suggestions on how to deal with the radioactive waste.

To date the White House has opposed utilities' calls for the government to build an interim storage site, fearing that it would divert resources from efforts to build a long-delayed permanent dump for the spent fuel.
Rep. Fred Upton, a Republican from Michigan who led efforts this year to pass a bill to build an interim storage site, urged the Energy Department to be more proactive in finding a solution.
He said Wednesday that he would reintroduce his bill, which had bipartisan support, early next year.
